Topic-11: Family Card - A Way of Poverty
                     Alleviation
Quotation
“The best way to help the poor is not to make them dependent on aid, but to
provide opportunities that allow them to live with dignity.”
—Simon johnson, Nobel Laureate Economist
Introduction
Poverty alleviation remains one of the most important development priorities for
Bangladesh. Despite significant economic progress over the last decades, millions
of people still struggle to meet their basic needs. Social safety net programs have
played an important role in supporting vulnerable populations. In this context, the
concept of a “Family Card” has emerged as a policy proposal to ensure targeted
welfare support for low-income households. The idea, often discussed in political
discourse including the BNP’s vision and the policy ideas of Tarique Rahman,
aims to identify poor families and provide them with direct support such as food
subsidies, healthcare benefits, and financial assistance. By using a family-based
identification system, the program seeks to ensure transparency, reduce leakage in
welfare distribution, and improve poverty reduction efforts.
Relevant Data on Poverty and Social Safety Nets (Bangladesh)
 Indicator                          Data                         Source
 Poverty Rate                       Around 18–19%                Bangladesh Bureau of
                                                                 Statistics
 Extreme Poverty Rate            Around 5–6%                     BBS
 Population Below Poverty Line About 30 million                  World Bank
                                 people
 Social Safety Net Programs      Over 120 programs         Ministry of Finance
 Budget Allocation for Safety    Around 2.5–3% of          Government of Bangladesh
 Nets                            GDP
 Target Beneficiaries            Millions of low-          Government Reports
                                 income households
These data show the importance of targeted social protection mechanisms in
reducing poverty.
    
                           

Prospects of Family Card System for Poverty Alleviation
1. Targeted Distribution of Welfare Support
The family card system can help identify poor households accurately. This ensures
that government assistance reaches the most vulnerable groups.
2. Reduction of Poverty and Inequality
Providing direct financial and food support to low-income families can reduce
income inequality. It also helps improve living standards among marginalized
populations.
3. Improved Transparency in Welfare Programs
Digital or identification-based family cards can reduce corruption and leakage.
Transparent systems ensure fair distribution of government resources.
4. Strengthening Social Safety Nets
Family cards can integrate multiple welfare programs under a single platform. This
coordination improves efficiency in social protection initiatives.
5. Supporting Food Security
Low-income families can receive subsidized food and essential commodities. This
helps protect households from rising living costs and inflation.
6. Promoting Inclusive Development
Family card programs ensure that vulnerable populations are not excluded from
development benefits. Inclusive policies strengthen social justice and national
stability.
7. Alignment with BNP Vision for Welfare Policies
Policy proposals discussed within BNP’s welfare vision, including ideas
highlighted by Tarique Rahman, emphasize strengthening social protection and
targeted assistance to poor households. The family card concept aims to modernize
welfare delivery and reduce poverty more effectively.
Challenges of Implementing the Family Card System

    
                           

1. Identification of Eligible Families
Accurate identification of poor households can be difficult. Errors in targeting may
exclude deserving beneficiaries or include non-eligible households.
2. Administrative Complexity
Implementing a nationwide family card system requires strong administrative
capacity. Coordination between different government agencies is necessary.
3. Risk of Political Influence
Social welfare programs may sometimes be influenced by political considerations.
Ensuring neutrality is essential for program credibility.
4. Financial Sustainability
Large-scale welfare programs require substantial government funding. Budget
constraints may affect long-term implementation.
5. Lack of Updated Socioeconomic Data
Outdated poverty data can lead to inaccurate beneficiary lists. Regular data updates
are necessary for effective targeting.
6. Technological and Infrastructure Limitations
Digital systems require reliable technological infrastructure and trained personnel.
Weak infrastructure may slow implementation.
7. Public Awareness and Accessibility Issues
Some vulnerable households may not fully understand how to access the program.
Lack of awareness may limit participation.
Recommendations
1. Developing a Reliable Beneficiary Database
A comprehensive national database of low-income families should be created. This
will help ensure accurate targeting of welfare benefits.
2. Using Digital Technology for Transparency

    
                           

Digital platforms and smart cards can improve monitoring and reduce corruption.
Technology enhances accountability in welfare distribution.
3. Ensuring Non-Political Implementation
The family card program should be managed through independent administrative
mechanisms. Neutral implementation strengthens public trust.
4. Integrating Multiple Social Protection Programs
Different welfare schemes should be coordinated under a unified system.
Integration improves efficiency and reduces duplication.
5. Strengthening Monitoring and Evaluation
Regular monitoring and evaluation can identify weaknesses and improve program
performance. Transparent evaluation ensures better policy outcomes.
6. Increasing Budget Allocation for Social Protection
Adequate funding is necessary for effective poverty alleviation programs.
Sustainable financing ensures long-term success.
7. Enhancing Public Awareness and Accessibility
Public awareness campaigns can inform citizens about eligibility and application
procedures. This ensures that vulnerable families benefit from the program.
Conclusion
The family card system represents a potential approach to improving poverty
alleviation and strengthening social safety nets in Bangladesh. By targeting support

### ফ্যামিলি কার্ড: দারিদ্র্য বিমোচনের নতুন কৌশল

> “The best way to help the poor is not to make them dependent on aid, but to
provide opportunities that allow them to live with dignity.”  
> — **Simon johnson, Nobel Laureate Economist**

## 1. Introduction & Context

Poverty alleviation remains one of the most important development priorities for Bangladesh. Despite significant economic progress over the last decades, millions of people still struggle to meet their basic needs. Social safety net programs have played an important role in supporting vulnerable populations. In this context, the concept of a “Family Card” has emerged as a policy proposal to ensure targeted welfare support for low-income households. The idea, often discussed in political discourse including the BNP’s vision and the policy ideas of Tarique Rahman, aims to identify poor families and provide them with direct support such as food subsidies, healthcare benefits, and financial assistance. By using a family-based identification system, the program seeks to ensure transparency, reduce leakage in welfare distribution, and improve poverty reduction efforts.

## 3. Prospects & Key Pillars

### 1. Targeted Distribution of Welfare Support
The family card system can help identify poor households accurately. This ensures that government assistance reaches the most vulnerable groups.

### 2. Reduction of Poverty and Inequality
Providing direct financial and food support to low-income families can reduce income inequality. It also helps improve living standards among marginalized populations.

### 3. Improved Transparency in Welfare Programs
Digital or identification-based family cards can reduce corruption and leakage. Transparent systems ensure fair distribution of government resources.

### 4. Strengthening Social Safety Nets
Family cards can integrate multiple welfare programs under a single platform. This coordination improves efficiency in social protection initiatives.

### 5. Supporting Food Security
Low-income families can receive subsidized food and essential commodities. This helps protect households from rising living costs and inflation.

### 6. Promoting Inclusive Development
Family card programs ensure that vulnerable populations are not excluded from development benefits. Inclusive policies strengthen social justice and national stability.

### 7. Alignment with BNP Vision for Welfare Policies
Policy proposals discussed within BNP’s welfare vision, including ideas highlighted by Tarique Rahman, emphasize strengthening social protection and targeted assistance to poor households. The family card concept aims to modernize welfare delivery and reduce poverty more effectively.

## 4. Key Challenges & Systemic Bottlenecks

### 1. Identification of Eligible Families
Accurate identification of poor households can be difficult. Errors in targeting may exclude deserving beneficiaries or include non-eligible households.

### 2. Administrative Complexity
Implementing a nationwide family card system requires strong administrative capacity. Coordination between different government agencies is necessary.

### 3. Risk of Political Influence
Social welfare programs may sometimes be influenced by political considerations. Ensuring neutrality is essential for program credibility.

### 4. Financial Sustainability
Large-scale welfare programs require substantial government funding. Budget constraints may affect long-term implementation.

### 5. Lack of Updated Socioeconomic Data
Outdated poverty data can lead to inaccurate beneficiary lists. Regular data updates are necessary for effective targeting.

### 6. Technological and Infrastructure Limitations
Digital systems require reliable technological infrastructure and trained personnel. Weak infrastructure may slow implementation.

### 7. Public Awareness and Accessibility Issues
Some vulnerable households may not fully understand how to access the program. Lack of awareness may limit participation.

## 5. Strategic Recommendations & Way Forward

### 1. Developing a Reliable Beneficiary Database
A comprehensive national database of low-income families should be created. This will help ensure accurate targeting of welfare benefits.

### 2. Using Digital Technology for Transparency
Digital platforms and smart cards can improve monitoring and reduce corruption. Technology enhances accountability in welfare distribution.

### 3. Ensuring Non-Political Implementation
The family card program should be managed through independent administrative mechanisms. Neutral implementation strengthens public trust.

### 4. Integrating Multiple Social Protection Programs
Different welfare schemes should be coordinated under a unified system. Integration improves efficiency and reduces duplication.

### 5. Strengthening Monitoring and Evaluation
Regular monitoring and evaluation can identify weaknesses and improve program performance. Transparent evaluation ensures better policy outcomes.

### 6. Increasing Budget Allocation for Social Protection
Adequate funding is necessary for effective poverty alleviation programs. Sustainable financing ensures long-term success.

### 7. Enhancing Public Awareness and Accessibility
Public awareness campaigns can inform citizens about eligibility and application procedures. This ensures that vulnerable families benefit from the program.

## 6. Conclusion

*The family card system represents a potential approach to improving poverty alleviation and strengthening social safety nets in Bangladesh. By targeting support to vulnerable households, the program can reduce inequality and improve living standards. Policy ideas associated with the BNP’s welfare vision and discussions by Tarique Rahman emphasize the importance of modernizing social protection systems and ensuring that assistance reaches those who need it most. > “A resilient, transparent financial system is the bedrock of sustainable economic growth.”  
> — **Bangladesh Bank / World Bank Policy Guidelines**

## 1. Introduction & Context

Corruption is widely considered one of the most significant obstacles to economic development, good governance, and social justice in many developing countries. It refers to the abuse of entrusted power for private gain, including bribery, embezzlement, nepotism, and misuse of public resources. In Bangladesh, corruption has been a persistent challenge affecting various sectors such as public administration, banking, procurement, and politics. Although the country has made progress in economic growth and poverty reduction, corruption continues to undermine institutional efficiency, discourage investment, and weaken public trust in governance. Addressing corruption is therefore essential for ensuring transparency, accountability, and sustainable development. Political visions and reform proposals from different parties—including discussions within BNP’s governance vision and the reform-oriented ideas emphasized by Tarique Rahman regarding accountability and institutional reform—often highlight the importance of strengthening anti-corruption measures and restoring transparent governance.

## 2. Relevant Economic Indicators

## 3. Prospects & Key Pillars

### 1. Strengthening Institutional Accountability
Improving the independence and effectiveness of oversight institutions can help detect and prevent corruption. Strong institutions ensure transparency in governance.

### 2. Digitalization of Government Services
Introducing e-governance systems reduces direct contact between citizens and officials. Digital services can minimize opportunities for bribery and administrative corruption.

### 3. Public Awareness and Civic Engagement
Greater public awareness about corruption and citizens’ rights can encourage people to demand accountability. Civic participation strengthens democratic governance.

### 4. Legal and Judicial Reforms
Modernizing anti-corruption laws and strengthening judicial independence can improve law enforcement. Effective legal systems deter corrupt practices.

### 5. International Cooperation Against Corruption
Global frameworks such as the UN Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC) support anti-corruption initiatives. International cooperation improves transparency and accountability.

### 6. Reform-Oriented Governance Vision
Policy discussions within political platforms—including BNP’s stated emphasis on institutional reform and accountability in governance—often highlight anti- corruption measures as a central priority.

### 7. Youth and Civil Society Participation
Young people and civil society organizations increasingly advocate for transparency and ethical governance. Their engagement can drive long-term reforms.

## 4. Key Challenges & Systemic Bottlenecks

### 1. Weak Institutional Enforcement
Although anti-corruption laws exist, enforcement is sometimes inconsistent. Weak institutional capacity may reduce the effectiveness of anti-corruption efforts.

### 2. Political Influence and Patronage
Political patronage systems can sometimes protect corrupt individuals. This undermines accountability and public trust.

### 3. Lack of Transparency in Public Procurement
Large government projects may face risks of irregularities in procurement processes. Lack of transparency increases opportunities for corruption.

### 4. Limited Judicial Efficiency
Delayed legal processes may discourage prosecution of corruption cases. Efficient judicial systems are essential for enforcing accountability.

### 5. Administrative Complexity and Bureaucracy
Complex procedures in public administration may encourage bribery or informal payments. Simplifying processes can reduce such risks.

### 6. Social Acceptance of Corrupt Practices
In some cases, bribery is viewed as a normal administrative shortcut. Changing social attitudes toward corruption is challenging.

### 7. Weak Protection for Whistleblowers
Individuals who expose corruption may face risks or retaliation. Lack of protection discourages reporting of corruption cases.

## 5. Strategic Recommendations & Way Forward

### 1. Strengthening the Anti-Corruption Commission
The Anti-Corruption Commission should operate independently and effectively. Strong investigative powers are necessary to combat corruption.

### 2. Promoting E-Governance and Digital Transparency
Expanding digital services in taxation, licensing, and procurement can reduce human discretion. Technology improves transparency and accountability.

### 3. Judicial and Legal Reforms
Strengthening judicial independence and speeding up corruption trials can ensure justice. Effective legal frameworks deter corrupt practices.

### 4. Enhancing Public Sector Accountability
Government officials should be required to disclose assets and financial interests. Transparency in public service builds trust.

### 5. Reforming Public Procurement Systems
Transparent and competitive procurement processes should be ensured. Independent monitoring can reduce irregularities.

### 6. Encouraging Ethical Leadership and Governance Reform
Policy discussions within different political visions—including BNP’s governance reform proposals often associated with Tarique Rahman’s emphasis on accountability and transparency—stress the need for institutional reforms to combat corruption.

### 7. Strengthening Civic Education and Public Awareness
Educational programs should promote ethical values and anti-corruption awareness. Public participation is vital for long-term governance reform.

## 6. Conclusion

*Corruption remains one of the major barriers to good governance and sustainable development in Bangladesh. While the country has achieved notable economic progress, corruption continues to undermine institutional efficiency, investor confidence, and public trust. Combating corruption requires comprehensive reforms, including stronger institutions, transparent governance systems, and active public participation. Reform-oriented governance visions discussed within various political platforms—including ideas emphasizing institutional accountability and transparency—highlight the importance of tackling corruption as a national priority. By strengthening democratic institutions and ensuring accountability, Bangladesh can build a more transparent, efficient, and just society. introduction: The digital economy refers to economic activities that are based on digital technologies such as the internet, mobile communication, digital platforms, data, and information technology. In recent years, Bangladesh has made remarkable progress in developing its digital economy through initiatives like “Digital Bangladesh.” The growth of internet connectivity, smartphone usage, digital financial services, e- commerce, freelancing, and ICT exports has contributed significantly to the country's economic transformation. The digital economy is helping Bangladesh create employment opportunities, improve public services, and promote innovation. With a young population and a rapidly growing technology sector, Bangladesh has the potential to become a strong digital economy in South Asia. However, achieving this goal requires addressing several challenges while strengthening digital infrastructure and skills.

prospects.title: Expansion of Internet Access
prospects.explanation: Internet usage in Bangladesh is growing rapidly. Increased connectivity allows more people to participate in online economic activities such as e-commerce and digital services.

prospects.title: Growth of E-commerce
prospects.explanation: Online shopping platforms have become very popular in Bangladesh. E-commerce businesses create employment opportunities and make products accessible to people across the country.

prospects.title: Rise of Digital Financial Services
prospects.explanation: Mobile banking and digital payment systems such as bKash and Nagad have transformed financial transactions. These services make financial activities easier, faster, and more secure.

prospects.title: Freelancing and Outsourcing Opportunities
prospects.explanation: Bangladesh is one of the leading countries in freelancing. Many young people are earning income from global markets through platforms like Upwork and Fiverr.

prospects.title: Development of ICT Industry
prospects.explanation: The ICT sector in Bangladesh is growing rapidly with software companies and tech startups emerging across the country. This sector contributes to export earnings and job creation.

prospects.title: Digital Government Services
prospects.explanation: Government services are becoming digital through e-governance initiatives. Citizens can now access many services online, reducing time and cost.

prospects.title: Youth Population Advantage
prospects.explanation: Bangladesh has a large young population who are tech-savvy and capable of adopting new digital technologies. This provides a strong workforce for the digital economy.

challenges.title: Digital Divide
challenges.explanation: Many rural areas still lack reliable internet access. This creates inequality in digital opportunities between urban and rural populations.

challenges.title: Lack of Skilled Workforce
challenges.explanation: Although many people use the internet, advanced digital skills such as programming, AI, and cybersecurity are still limited.

challenges.title: Cybersecurity Risks
challenges.explanation: As digital activities increase, the risk of cybercrime, data breaches, and online fraud also increases.

challenges.title: Limited Digital Infrastructure
challenges.explanation: Some areas still experience slow internet speed and unstable connectivity, which affects digital business operations.

challenges.title: Regulatory Barriers
challenges.explanation: Complicated regulations and policies sometimes make it difficult for startups and digital businesses to grow.

challenges.title: Low Investment in Technology
challenges.explanation: Investment in research, development, and innovation is still relatively low compared to developed digital economies.

Topic-13: Digital Economy in Bangladesh
“A thriving digital economy fuels job creation, fosters innovation, and
accelerates sustainable development.” — World Bank

Introduction
The digital economy refers to economic activities that are based on digital
technologies such as the internet, mobile communication, digital platforms, data, and
information technology. In recent years, Bangladesh has made remarkable progress
in developing its digital economy through initiatives like “Digital Bangladesh.”

The growth of internet connectivity, smartphone usage, digital financial services, e-
commerce, freelancing, and ICT exports has contributed significantly to the
country's economic transformation. The digital economy is helping Bangladesh
create employment opportunities, improve public services, and promote innovation.

With a young population and a rapidly growing technology sector, Bangladesh has
the potential to become a strong digital economy in South Asia. However, achieving
this goal requires addressing several challenges while strengthening digital
infrastructure and skills.

Relative Data
                    Indicator                             Data                  Year
   Population                                  175 million                  2025
   Internet Users                              77.7 million                 2025
   Internet Penetration                        44.5%                        2025
   Mobile Connections                          185 million                  2025
   Social Media Users                          60 million                   2025
   GDP                                         $450 billion                 2024

     
                            

   ICT Service Exports                         $702 million                 2024
Prospects of Digital Economy in Bangladesh
1. Expansion of Internet Access

Internet usage in Bangladesh is growing rapidly. Increased connectivity allows more
people to participate in online economic activities such as e-commerce and digital
services.

2. Growth of E-commerce

Online shopping platforms have become very popular in Bangladesh. E-commerce
businesses create employment opportunities and make products accessible to people
across the country.

3. Rise of Digital Financial Services

Mobile banking and digital payment systems such as bKash and Nagad have
transformed financial transactions. These services make financial activities easier,
faster, and more secure.

4. Freelancing and Outsourcing Opportunities

Bangladesh is one of the leading countries in freelancing. Many young people are
earning income from global markets through platforms like Upwork and Fiverr.

5. Development of ICT Industry

The ICT sector in Bangladesh is growing rapidly with software companies and tech
startups emerging across the country. This sector contributes to export earnings and
job creation.

6. Digital Government Services


     
                            

Government services are becoming digital through e-governance initiatives. Citizens
can now access many services online, reducing time and cost.

7. Youth Population Advantage

Bangladesh has a large young population who are tech-savvy and capable of
adopting new digital technologies. This provides a strong workforce for the digital
economy.

Challenges of Digital Economy
1. Digital Divide

Many rural areas still lack reliable internet access. This creates inequality in digital
opportunities between urban and rural populations.

2. Lack of Skilled Workforce

Although many people use the internet, advanced digital skills such as programming,
AI, and cybersecurity are still limited.

3. Cybersecurity Risks

As digital activities increase, the risk of cybercrime, data breaches, and online fraud
also increases.

4. Limited Digital Infrastructure

Some areas still experience slow internet speed and unstable connectivity, which
affects digital business operations.

5. Regulatory Barriers

Complicated regulations and policies sometimes make it difficult for startups and
digital businesses to grow.

     
                             

6. Low Investment in Technology

Investment in research, development, and innovation is still relatively low compared
to developed digital economies.

7. Export Limitations

Although ICT exports are increasing, Bangladesh still needs to produce more high-
value digital products and services.

Recommendations
1. Improve Digital Infrastructure

The government should expand high-speed internet across the country, especially in
rural areas.

2. Develop Digital Skills

Educational institutions should provide training in programming, data science, AI,
and other digital skills.

3. Strengthen Cybersecurity

Strong cybersecurity systems and awareness programs are necessary to protect
digital platforms and users.

4. Support Startups

Providing financial support, incubation programs, and favorable policies can help
digital startups grow.

5. Encourage ICT Investment

Both public and private sectors should increase investment in technology and
innovation.
     
                            

6. Promote Digital Inclusion

Policies should ensure that women, rural communities, and disadvantaged groups
have access to digital opportunities.

7. Expand ICT Export Markets

Bangladesh should focus on exporting high-value digital products and services to
global markets.

Conclusion
The digital economy is becoming a key driver of economic growth in Bangladesh.
With increasing internet penetration, digital services, and a young workforce, the
country has significant potential to expand its digital sector.

However, to fully realize this potential, Bangladesh must address challenges such as
digital inequality, skill shortages, and cybersecurity risks. By investing in
infrastructure, education, and innovation, Bangladesh can build a strong and
sustainable digital economy that benefits all citizens.




     
                           

Related Quotations
“The digital economy is the new engine of global growth.” — OECD

“Technology is best when it brings people together.” — Matt Mullenweg

“The future of economic growth lies in digital transformation.” — World
Economic Forum

> “A resilient, transparent financial system is the bedrock of sustainable economic growth.”

## 1. Introduction & Context

The digital economy refers to economic activities that are based on digital technologies such as the internet, mobile communication, digital platforms, data, and information technology. In recent years, Bangladesh has made remarkable progress in developing its digital economy through initiatives like “Digital Bangladesh.” The growth of internet connectivity, smartphone usage, digital financial services, e- commerce, freelancing, and ICT exports has contributed significantly to the country's economic transformation. The digital economy is helping Bangladesh create employment opportunities, improve public services, and promote innovation. With a young population and a rapidly growing technology sector, Bangladesh has the potential to become a strong digital economy in South Asia. However, achieving this goal requires addressing several challenges while strengthening digital infrastructure and skills.

## 2. Relevant Economic Indicators

## 3. Prospects & Key Pillars

### 1. Expansion of Internet Access
Internet usage in Bangladesh is growing rapidly. Increased connectivity allows more people to participate in online economic activities such as e-commerce and digital services.

### 2. Growth of E-commerce
Online shopping platforms have become very popular in Bangladesh. E-commerce businesses create employment opportunities and make products accessible to people across the country.

### 3. Rise of Digital Financial Services
Mobile banking and digital payment systems such as bKash and Nagad have transformed financial transactions. These services make financial activities easier, faster, and more secure.

### 4. Freelancing and Outsourcing Opportunities
Bangladesh is one of the leading countries in freelancing. Many young people are earning income from global markets through platforms like Upwork and Fiverr.

### 5. Development of ICT Industry
The ICT sector in Bangladesh is growing rapidly with software companies and tech startups emerging across the country. This sector contributes to export earnings and job creation.

### 6. Digital Government Services
Government services are becoming digital through e-governance initiatives. Citizens can now access many services online, reducing time and cost.

### 7. Youth Population Advantage
Bangladesh has a large young population who are tech-savvy and capable of adopting new digital technologies. This provides a strong workforce for the digital economy.

## 4. Key Challenges & Systemic Bottlenecks

### 1. Digital Divide
Many rural areas still lack reliable internet access. This creates inequality in digital opportunities between urban and rural populations.

### 2. Lack of Skilled Workforce
Although many people use the internet, advanced digital skills such as programming, AI, and cybersecurity are still limited.

### 3. Cybersecurity Risks
As digital activities increase, the risk of cybercrime, data breaches, and online fraud also increases.

### 4. Limited Digital Infrastructure
Some areas still experience slow internet speed and unstable connectivity, which affects digital business operations.

### 5. Regulatory Barriers
Complicated regulations and policies sometimes make it difficult for startups and digital businesses to grow.

### 6. Low Investment in Technology
Investment in research, development, and innovation is still relatively low compared to developed digital economies.

### 7. Export Limitations
Although ICT exports are increasing, Bangladesh still needs to produce more high- value digital products and services.

## 5. Strategic Recommendations & Way Forward

### 1. Improve Digital Infrastructure
The government should expand high-speed internet across the country, especially in rural areas.

### 2. Develop Digital Skills
Educational institutions should provide training in programming, data science, AI, and other digital skills.

### 3. Strengthen Cybersecurity
Strong cybersecurity systems and awareness programs are necessary to protect digital platforms and users.

### 4. Support Startups
Providing financial support, incubation programs, and favorable policies can help digital startups grow.

### 5. Encourage ICT Investment
Both public and private sectors should increase investment in technology and innovation.

### 6. Promote Digital Inclusion
Policies should ensure that women, rural communities, and disadvantaged groups have access to digital opportunities.

### 7. Expand ICT Export Markets
Bangladesh should focus on exporting high-value digital products and services to global markets.

## 6. Conclusion

*The digital economy is becoming a key driver of economic growth in Bangladesh. With increasing internet penetration, digital services, and a young workforce, the country has significant potential to expand its digital sector. However, to fully realize this potential, Bangladesh must address challenges such as digital inequality, skill shortages, and cybersecurity risks. By investing in infrastructure, education, and innovation, Bangladesh can build a strong and sustainable digital economy that benefits all citizens. Related Quotations “The digital economy is the new engine of global growth.” — OECD “Technology is best when it brings people together.” — Matt Mullenweg “The future of economic growth lies in digital transformation.” — World Economic Forum*

Topic-14: AI and Cybersecurity for the Banking
                    Sector
Quotation
“Artificial Intelligence will be the key technology to strengthen cybersecurity in
financial institutions as cyber threats become more sophisticated.”
— World Economic Forum, Global Cybersecurity Outlook (2023)

Reference: World Economic Forum. (2023). Global Cybersecurity Outlook Report.

Introduction
The banking sector has become one of the most targeted industries for cybercrime
due to the high value of financial data and digital transactions. With the rapid
growth of online banking, mobile payments, and digital financial services,
traditional cybersecurity methods are often insufficient to combat increasingly
sophisticated cyber threats. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful
solution to enhance cybersecurity in banking systems.

AI-driven cybersecurity systems can detect anomalies, identify fraud patterns, and
respond to threats in real time. By analyzing massive volumes of transaction data
and network activities, AI technologies enable banks to strengthen their defenses
against cyber attacks such as phishing, ransomware, identity theft, and financial
fraud. As cyber threats continue to evolve, integrating AI with cybersecurity
strategies is becoming essential for modern banking infrastructure.




    
                              

  Relative Data
 Global Cyber Attacks in Banking Sector
Year            Percentage of Cyber Attacks Targeting Financial Institutions
2019                         18%
2020                         23%
2021                         28%
2022                         31%
2023                         34%
 Source: IBM Security X-Force Threat Intelligence Index (2024)
 Fraud Detection Improvement Using AI

                        Technology                 Fraud Detection Accuracy
             Traditional Rule-Based Systems                65%
             Machine Learning Systems                      85%
             Advanced AI Models                            95%
 Source: Deloitte Financial Cybersecurity Report (2023)

 Prospects of AI in Banking Cybersecurity
 1. Real-Time Fraud Detection

 AI systems analyze transaction data instantly to detect suspicious patterns and
 block fraudulent activities. This allows banks to prevent financial losses before
 they occur.

 2. Automated Threat Detection

 AI can monitor networks continuously and identify cyber threats automatically. It
 reduces the need for manual monitoring and improves response time.


       
                            

3. Improved Risk Management

AI tools can analyze historical and real-time data to predict potential cyber risks.
Banks can take preventive measures before attacks occur.

4. Behavioral Biometrics

AI analyzes user behavior such as typing patterns and login habits. This helps
identify unauthorized access attempts even if login credentials are stolen.

5. Enhanced Fraud Analytics

Machine learning algorithms identify hidden fraud patterns across millions of
transactions. This improves the accuracy of fraud detection systems.

6. Efficient Incident Response

AI can automate responses to cyber incidents by isolating compromised systems.
This reduces the time required to control cyber attacks.

7. Cost Reduction in Security Operations

AI reduces manual security operations by automating threat detection and analysis.
This helps banks reduce operational costs while maintaining high security
standards.

Challenges of AI in Banking Cybersecurity
1. High Implementation Cost

Implementing AI-based cybersecurity systems requires significant investment in
technology infrastructure and skilled professionals.

2. Data Privacy Concerns



     
                            

Banks handle sensitive customer data, and AI systems must comply with strict
privacy regulations to protect user information.

3. Complex Integration with Legacy Systems

Many banks still use outdated IT systems. Integrating AI solutions with these
legacy systems can be technically challenging.

4. Risk of AI-Based Cyber Attacks

Cybercriminals are also using AI technologies to launch more sophisticated
attacks. This creates a continuous technological arms race.

5. Lack of Skilled Professionals

There is a shortage of experts in AI-driven cybersecurity. Banks often struggle to
recruit professionals with the required expertise.

6. Algorithm Bias and Errors

AI models may produce incorrect predictions if trained on biased or insufficient
data. This can lead to false security alerts.

7. Regulatory and Compliance Issues

Financial institutions must follow strict regulations. Implementing AI solutions
requires compliance with multiple cybersecurity and financial laws.

Recommendations
1. Invest in Advanced AI Security Systems

Banks should adopt advanced AI-driven cybersecurity platforms to detect and
respond to threats effectively.

2. Strengthen Data Governance
     
                            

Financial institutions must implement strict data protection policies to ensure
customer data privacy and regulatory compliance.

3. Develop Skilled Cybersecurity Workforce

Banks should train employees and hire specialists in AI and cybersecurity to
manage advanced security systems.

4. Upgrade Legacy IT Infrastructure

Modernizing outdated banking systems will make it easier to integrate AI-based
cybersecurity solutions.

5. Collaborate with Technology Firms

Banks should partner with cybersecurity companies and fintech organizations to
develop innovative security solutions.

6. Continuous Monitoring and Updating

AI security systems should be regularly updated with new threat intelligence to
remain effective against evolving cyber attacks.

7. Implement Multi-Layer Security Strategy

Combining AI with traditional security tools such as firewalls, encryption, and
authentication systems provides stronger protection.

Conclusion
Artificial Intelligence is transforming cybersecurity in the banking sector by
providing advanced tools for detecting, preventing, and responding to cyber
threats. As digital banking continues to expand, financial institutions must adopt
AI-driven security solutions to protect sensitive financial data and maintain


    
                            

customer trust. Despite several challenges, strategic investment, skilled workforce
development, and proper regulatory compliance can enable banks to fully leverage
the benefits of AI in cybersecurity. Ultimately, integrating AI into banking security
frameworks will play a critical role in building a resilient and secure financial
ecosystem.

Additional Related Quotations

— Stephane Nappo, Global Chief Information Security Officer

“Artificial intelligence is the new electricity powering the future of cybersecurity.”
— Andrew Ng, AI Researcher

systems from evolving cyber threats.”

## 1. Introduction & Context

The banking sector has become one of the most targeted industries for cybercrime due to the high value of financial data and digital transactions. With the rapid growth of online banking, mobile payments, and digital financial services, traditional cybersecurity methods are often insufficient to combat increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful solution to enhance cybersecurity in banking systems. AI-driven cybersecurity systems can detect anomalies, identify fraud patterns, and respond to threats in real time. By analyzing massive volumes of transaction data and network activities, AI technologies enable banks to strengthen their defenses against cyber attacks such as phishing, ransomware, identity theft, and financial fraud. As cyber threats continue to evolve, integrating AI with cybersecurity strategies is becoming essential for modern banking infrastructure.

## 2. Relevant Economic Indicators

| অর্থনৈতিক নির্দেশক (Indicator) | সাম্প্রতিক উপাত্ত (Data / Figure) | অফিসিয়াল উৎস (Source) |

## 3. Prospects & Key Pillars

### 1. Real-Time Fraud Detection
AI systems analyze transaction data instantly to detect suspicious patterns and block fraudulent activities. This allows banks to prevent financial losses before they occur.

### 2. Automated Threat Detection
AI can monitor networks continuously and identify cyber threats automatically. It reduces the need for manual monitoring and improves response time.

### 3. Improved Risk Management
AI tools can analyze historical and real-time data to predict potential cyber risks. Banks can take preventive measures before attacks occur.

### 4. Behavioral Biometrics
AI analyzes user behavior such as typing patterns and login habits. This helps identify unauthorized access attempts even if login credentials are stolen.

### 5. Enhanced Fraud Analytics
Machine learning algorithms identify hidden fraud patterns across millions of transactions. This improves the accuracy of fraud detection systems.

### 6. Efficient Incident Response
AI can automate responses to cyber incidents by isolating compromised systems. This reduces the time required to control cyber attacks.

### 7. Cost Reduction in Security Operations
AI reduces manual security operations by automating threat detection and analysis. This helps banks reduce operational costs while maintaining high security standards.

## 4. Key Challenges & Systemic Bottlenecks

### 1. High Implementation Cost
Implementing AI-based cybersecurity systems requires significant investment in technology infrastructure and skilled professionals.

### 2. Data Privacy Concerns
Banks handle sensitive customer data, and AI systems must comply with strict privacy regulations to protect user information.

### 3. Complex Integration with Legacy Systems
Many banks still use outdated IT systems. Integrating AI solutions with these legacy systems can be technically challenging.

### 4. Risk of AI-Based Cyber Attacks
Cybercriminals are also using AI technologies to launch more sophisticated attacks. This creates a continuous technological arms race.

### 5. Lack of Skilled Professionals
There is a shortage of experts in AI-driven cybersecurity. Banks often struggle to recruit professionals with the required expertise.

### 6. Algorithm Bias and Errors
AI models may produce incorrect predictions if trained on biased or insufficient data. This can lead to false security alerts.

### 7. Regulatory and Compliance Issues
Financial institutions must follow strict regulations. Implementing AI solutions requires compliance with multiple cybersecurity and financial laws.

## 5. Strategic Recommendations & Way Forward

### 1. Invest in Advanced AI Security Systems
Banks should adopt advanced AI-driven cybersecurity platforms to detect and respond to threats effectively.

### 2. Strengthen Data Governance
Financial institutions must implement strict data protection policies to ensure customer data privacy and regulatory compliance.

### 3. Develop Skilled Cybersecurity Workforce
Banks should train employees and hire specialists in AI and cybersecurity to manage advanced security systems.

### 4. Upgrade Legacy IT Infrastructure
Modernizing outdated banking systems will make it easier to integrate AI-based cybersecurity solutions.

### 5. Collaborate with Technology Firms
Banks should partner with cybersecurity companies and fintech organizations to develop innovative security solutions.

### 6. Continuous Monitoring and Updating
AI security systems should be regularly updated with new threat intelligence to remain effective against evolving cyber attacks.

### 7. Implement Multi-Layer Security Strategy
Combining AI with traditional security tools such as firewalls, encryption, and authentication systems provides stronger protection.

## 6. Conclusion

*Artificial Intelligence is transforming cybersecurity in the banking sector by providing advanced tools for detecting, preventing, and responding to cyber threats. As digital banking continues to expand, financial institutions must adopt AI-driven security solutions to protect sensitive financial data and maintain customer trust. Despite several challenges, strategic investment, skilled workforce development, and proper regulatory compliance can enable banks to fully leverage the benefits of AI in cybersecurity. Ultimately, integrating AI into banking security frameworks will play a critical role in building a resilient and secure financial ecosystem. Topic-15: The Power of Youth in Nation Building
Opening Quotation

“The youth of today are the leaders of tomorrow.”
— Nelson Mandela, Former President of South Africa

Introduction

Youth represent the most energetic, creative, and dynamic segment of any nation.
Their ideas, enthusiasm, and ability to adapt to change make them a crucial force
in shaping the future of society. In many developing countries, especially in South
Asia, a large proportion of the population consists of young people. This
demographic advantage can significantly accelerate economic growth, social
progress, and political stability when properly guided and empowered.

Nation building requires innovation, productivity, and a strong sense of
responsibility—qualities that youth naturally possess. By engaging in education,
entrepreneurship, technological innovation, and social initiatives, young people can
contribute to national development. Therefore, investing in youth development is
not merely a social responsibility but a strategic necessity for sustainable progress.

Youth Demographics and Development Data

Global Youth Population Overview

             Indicator                       Data                      Source
 Global youth population (15–24 ~1.2 billion                 United Nations (UN
 years)                                                     DESA)
 Percentage of world population       Around 16%             UN World Youth Report
 Youth in developing countries        Nearly 90%             United Nations

     
                           

 Youth unemployment rate             About 13%              International Labour
 worldwide                                                 Organization (ILO)
Source: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN
DESA), International Labour Organization (ILO), World Youth Report.

Youth Contribution to Economic Growth (Example Trend)

                      Sector               Youth Participation Impact
             Technology & Innovation       Startups, digital solutions
             Entrepreneurship              Small and medium enterprises
             Education & Research          Knowledge development
             Social Development            Volunteerism and activism
Source: World Bank Youth Development Indicators.

Prospects of Youth in Nation Building
1. Innovation and Creativity

Young people are naturally innovative and open to new ideas. Their creativity
helps develop new technologies, business models, and social solutions that drive
national development.

2. Technological Advancement

Youth adapt quickly to digital tools and modern technology. Their involvement in
IT, AI, and digital platforms accelerates economic modernization.

3. Entrepreneurship Growth

Young entrepreneurs create startups and businesses that generate employment. This
reduces unemployment and strengthens the national economy.

4. Social Reform and Awareness
    
                           

Youth often lead social movements and campaigns for justice, equality, and
sustainability. Their activism helps shape progressive and inclusive societies.

5. Human Capital Development

With proper education and skills training, youth become highly productive human
resources. Skilled young workers increase a country's competitiveness globally.

6. Political Participation

Youth participation in governance encourages democratic values and
accountability. Young leaders often introduce fresh perspectives to political
systems.

7. Nation’s Future Leadership

Today's youth will become tomorrow’s policymakers, scientists, and innovators.
Preparing them today ensures sustainable leadership in the future.

Challenges Faced by Youth in Nation Building

1. Unemployment

Many young people struggle to find jobs due to limited opportunities. Youth
unemployment slows economic development and causes frustration.

2. Lack of Quality Education

In many regions, education systems fail to provide practical skills. This creates a
mismatch between academic learning and job market demands.

3. Limited Access to Resources

Young entrepreneurs often lack financial support and resources. Without funding
and mentorship, innovative ideas may never be realized.

    
                            

4. Social and Cultural Barriers

Traditional norms sometimes restrict youth participation in decision-making. This
limits their ability to contribute effectively to society.

5. Political Manipulation

Youth may sometimes be used as tools in political conflicts. This can divert their
energy away from constructive nation-building activities.

6. Mental Health Issues

Pressure from unemployment, social expectations, and uncertainty affects youth
mental health. Poor mental wellbeing reduces productivity and engagement.

7. Digital Divide

Not all youth have equal access to technology and the internet. This inequality
prevents many from benefiting from digital opportunities.

Recommendations

1. Improve Education Systems

Governments should focus on practical and skill-based education. Modern
curricula aligned with industry needs will make youth more employable.

2. Promote Youth Entrepreneurship

Providing startup funding, training, and mentorship programs can encourage young
entrepreneurs. This will stimulate innovation and job creation.

3. Create Employment Opportunities




     
                           

Public and private sectors must collaborate to generate more job opportunities.
Youth-focused employment policies can strengthen economic growth.

4. Encourage Youth Participation in Governance

Young people should be involved in policymaking and leadership roles. Their
perspectives can help address modern social challenges effectively.

5. Invest in Technology and Digital Skills

Training programs in coding, AI, and digital literacy will prepare youth for the
future economy. Digital empowerment expands opportunities globally.

6. Strengthen Youth Support Programs

Governments and organizations should provide counseling, mentorship, and career
guidance. These programs help youth navigate challenges and achieve their goals.

7. Promote Volunteerism and Community Engagement

Encouraging youth participation in community service builds social responsibility.
Active engagement fosters unity and national pride.

Conclusion

Youth are the backbone of any nation's progress. Their energy, creativity, and
determination have the power to transform societies and shape a brighter future.
However, to fully harness this potential, governments, institutions, and
communities must invest in youth development through education, employment
opportunities, and empowerment programs. When young people are supported and
guided effectively, they become powerful agents of positive change. Thus,
empowering youth today ensures a stronger, more prosperous nation tomorrow.


    
                            

Additional Quotations

“Young people are the architects of the future.”
— Franklin D. Roosevelt

“Youth is not a time of life; it is a state of mind.”
— Samuel Ullman

“The future belongs to those who believe in the beauty of their dreams.”
— Eleanor Roosevelt

Topic-16: The Prospect of Outsourcing in
                     Bangladesh
Quotation
“Bangladesh has emerged as a promising destination for outsourcing due to its
large pool of young, skilled and cost-competitive workforce.”
— World Bank, Bangladesh Digital Economy Report (2022)
Reference: World Bank. (2022). Bangladesh Digital Economy Diagnostic Report.
Introduction
Outsourcing has become a significant driver of economic growth in many
developing countries, and Bangladesh is emerging as one of the promising
outsourcing hubs in the global market. With rapid technological advancement, the
expansion of internet connectivity, and a growing number of skilled young
professionals, Bangladesh is gaining international attention in the outsourcing
industry.
The country’s Information and Communication Technology (ICT) sector has
experienced steady growth over the past decade. Government initiatives such as
“Digital Bangladesh” and the development of IT parks have encouraged
freelancers and outsourcing companies to expand their services globally.
Outsourcing not only contributes to foreign currency earnings but also creates
employment opportunities for thousands of young people. As global companies
continue to search for cost-effective and skilled service providers, Bangladesh has
strong potential to become a leading outsourcing destination.




     
                              

Relative Data
Freelancers and Outsourcing Growth in Bangladesh
Year     Number of Freelancers               Earnings from Outsourcing (USD)
2021                  500,000                                  $100 million
2022                  600,000                                  $150 million
2023                  650,000                                  $200 million
2024                  700,000                                  $250 million
2025                 750,000+                                 $300 million+
Source: ICT Division Bangladesh & BASIS Report (2025)
Bangladesh’s Position in Global Freelancing

                                 Indicator                  Ranking
                      Global Freelancing Workforce        2nd Largest
                      IT Outsourcing Growth Rate          22% annually
                      Young Workforce (Under 35)          Over 60%
Source: Oxford Internet Institute Online Labour Index (2023)

Prospects of Outsourcing in Bangladesh

1. Large Young Workforce

Bangladesh has a large population of young people who are interested in
technology and freelancing. This workforce can easily adapt to digital skills
required in outsourcing industries.

2. Cost Competitive Services

Labor costs in Bangladesh are significantly lower compared to many developed
countries. This allows global companies to outsource tasks at affordable rates.


       
                           

3. Government Support for ICT Sector

The government has launched initiatives such as Digital Bangladesh and
established IT parks. These programs encourage the growth of outsourcing
businesses and freelancers.

4. Growing Internet Penetration

Improved internet infrastructure and high-speed connectivity enable freelancers to
work with international clients. This connectivity helps expand outsourcing
opportunities.

5. Expanding Global Demand

Companies worldwide are increasingly outsourcing services such as software
development, graphic design, and customer support. Bangladesh can capture a
large share of this growing market.

6. Rise of Freelancing Platforms

Platforms like Upwork, Fiverr, and Freelancer have opened opportunities for
Bangladeshi professionals to connect with global clients. This makes outsourcing
accessible even to individuals.

7. Increasing ICT Education

Many universities and training institutes are offering ICT-related programs. These
programs prepare students with technical skills required for outsourcing industries.

Challenges of Outsourcing in Bangladesh

1. Lack of Advanced Skills



    
                           

Although many freelancers are available, there is still a shortage of highly
specialized technical skills. This limits Bangladesh’s ability to compete in high-
value outsourcing projects.

2. Inconsistent Internet Connectivity

In some regions, internet speed and reliability remain unstable. This can disrupt
communication and project delivery for international clients.

3. Payment and Banking Limitations

Freelancers often face difficulties receiving international payments. Limited access
to global payment systems can discourage outsourcing activities.

4. Limited Awareness and Training

Many potential workers lack proper training or awareness about outsourcing
opportunities. Without guidance, they cannot effectively enter the global
freelancing market.

5. Cybersecurity Risks

Handling international data and projects requires strong cybersecurity measures.
Weak security systems can create trust issues with foreign clients.

6. Lack of Professional Communication Skills

English communication skills are sometimes limited among freelancers. This can
create misunderstandings with international clients.

7. Global Competition




    
                           

Countries like India, Philippines, and Vietnam are strong competitors in the
outsourcing industry. Bangladesh must improve quality and service standards to
compete globally.

Recommendations

1. Improve ICT Education and Training

Educational institutions should provide practical training in programming, digital
marketing, and software development. This will help create a skilled workforce for
outsourcing.

2. Strengthen Internet Infrastructure

The government should expand high-speed internet access across the country.
Reliable connectivity is essential for global outsourcing services.

3. Simplify International Payment Systems

Banks and financial institutions should develop easier payment solutions for
freelancers. This will encourage more people to join the outsourcing sector.

4. Promote Skill Development Programs

Training centers should offer courses in freelancing platforms and digital skills.
This will help new freelancers enter the global market more confidently.

5. Enhance English Communication Skills

Language training programs should be introduced to improve communication with
international clients. Effective communication increases client satisfaction.

6. Encourage Startup and IT Companies



    
                            

Government incentives and funding should support IT startups and outsourcing
companies. This will help expand the industry and create more employment
opportunities.

7. Improve Cybersecurity Framework

Strong cybersecurity policies should be implemented to protect client data. Secure
systems increase international trust in Bangladeshi outsourcing services.

Conclusion

Outsourcing has become an important sector for economic development in
Bangladesh. With a young workforce, government support, and growing
technological infrastructure, the country has great potential to become a global
outsourcing hub. However, challenges such as skill gaps, payment issues, and
infrastructure limitations must be addressed to fully utilize this opportunity. By
investing in education, improving connectivity, and strengthening policy support,
Bangladesh can significantly expand its presence in the global outsourcing market
and create sustainable employment for millions of people.

Additional Related Quotations

“Outsourcing is not just about reducing cost; it is about accessing global talent.”
— Thomas H. Davenport, Harvard Business Review

“Digital skills and freelancing opportunities can transform developing economies
like Bangladesh.”
— Oxford Internet Institute Report (2023)




     
                           

“The future workforce will increasingly work beyond borders through digital
outsourcing.”
— International Labour Organization (ILO)

# Topic 16: The Prospect of Outsourcing in Bangladesh
### বাংলাদেশে আউটসোর্সিং ও ফ্রিল্যান্সিং সম্ভাবনা

> “Bangladesh has emerged as a promising destination for outsourcing due to its
large pool of young, skilled and cost-competitive workforce.”  
> — **World Bank, Bangladesh Digital Economy Report (2022)
Reference: World Bank. (2022). Bangladesh Digital Economy Diagnostic Report.**

## 1. Introduction & Context

Outsourcing has become a significant driver of economic growth in many developing countries, and Bangladesh is emerging as one of the promising outsourcing hubs in the global market. With rapid technological advancement, the expansion of internet connectivity, and a growing number of skilled young professionals, Bangladesh is gaining international attention in the outsourcing industry. The country’s Information and Communication Technology (ICT) sector has experienced steady growth over the past decade. Government initiatives such as “Digital Bangladesh” and the development of IT parks have encouraged freelancers and outsourcing companies to expand their services globally. Outsourcing not only contributes to foreign currency earnings but also creates employment opportunities for thousands of young people. As global companies continue to search for cost-effective and skilled service providers, Bangladesh has strong potential to become a leading outsourcing destination.

## 2. Relevant Economic Indicators

| অর্থনৈতিক নির্দেশক (Indicator) | সাম্প্রতিক উপাত্ত (Data / Figure) | অফিসিয়াল উৎস (Source) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Year** | `Number of Freelancers` | Earnings from Outsourcing (USD) |
| **2021** | `500,000` | $100 million |
| **2022** | `600,000` | $150 million |
| **2023** | `650,000` | $200 million |
| **2024** | `700,000` | $250 million |
| **2025** | `750,000+` | $300 million+ |
| **Indicator** | `Ranking` | Bangladesh Bank / BBS |
| **Global Freelancing Workforce** | `2nd Largest` | Bangladesh Bank / BBS |
| **IT Outsourcing Growth Rate** | `22% annually` | Bangladesh Bank / BBS |
| **Young Workforce (Under 35)** | `Over 60%` | Bangladesh Bank / BBS |

## 3. Prospects & Key Pillars

### 1. Large Young Workforce
Bangladesh has a large population of young people who are interested in technology and freelancing. This workforce can easily adapt to digital skills required in outsourcing industries.

### 2. Cost Competitive Services
Labor costs in Bangladesh are significantly lower compared to many developed countries. This allows global companies to outsource tasks at affordable rates.

### 3. Government Support for ICT Sector
The government has launched initiatives such as Digital Bangladesh and established IT parks. These programs encourage the growth of outsourcing businesses and freelancers.

### 4. Growing Internet Penetration
Improved internet infrastructure and high-speed connectivity enable freelancers to work with international clients. This connectivity helps expand outsourcing opportunities.

### 5. Expanding Global Demand
Companies worldwide are increasingly outsourcing services such as software development, graphic design, and customer support. Bangladesh can capture a large share of this growing market.

### 6. Rise of Freelancing Platforms
Platforms like Upwork, Fiverr, and Freelancer have opened opportunities for Bangladeshi professionals to connect with global clients. This makes outsourcing accessible even to individuals.

### 7. Increasing ICT Education
Many universities and training institutes are offering ICT-related programs. These programs prepare students with technical skills required for outsourcing industries.

## 4. Key Challenges & Systemic Bottlenecks

### 1. Lack of Advanced Skills
Although many freelancers are available, there is still a shortage of highly specialized technical skills. This limits Bangladesh’s ability to compete in high- value outsourcing projects.

### 2. Inconsistent Internet Connectivity
In some regions, internet speed and reliability remain unstable. This can disrupt communication and project delivery for international clients.

### 3. Payment and Banking Limitations
Freelancers often face difficulties receiving international payments. Limited access to global payment systems can discourage outsourcing activities.

### 4. Limited Awareness and Training
Many potential workers lack proper training or awareness about outsourcing opportunities. Without guidance, they cannot effectively enter the global freelancing market.

### 5. Cybersecurity Risks
Handling international data and projects requires strong cybersecurity measures. Weak security systems can create trust issues with foreign clients.

### 6. Lack of Professional Communication Skills
English communication skills are sometimes limited among freelancers. This can create misunderstandings with international clients.

### 7. Global Competition
Countries like India, Philippines, and Vietnam are strong competitors in the outsourcing industry. Bangladesh must improve quality and service standards to compete globally.

## 5. Strategic Recommendations & Way Forward

### 1. Improve ICT Education and Training
Educational institutions should provide practical training in programming, digital marketing, and software development. This will help create a skilled workforce for outsourcing.

### 2. Strengthen Internet Infrastructure
The government should expand high-speed internet access across the country. Reliable connectivity is essential for global outsourcing services.

### 3. Simplify International Payment Systems
Banks and financial institutions should develop easier payment solutions for freelancers. This will encourage more people to join the outsourcing sector.

### 4. Promote Skill Development Programs
Training centers should offer courses in freelancing platforms and digital skills. This will help new freelancers enter the global market more confidently.

### 5. Enhance English Communication Skills
Language training programs should be introduced to improve communication with international clients. Effective communication increases client satisfaction.

### 6. Encourage Startup and IT Companies
Government incentives and funding should support IT startups and outsourcing companies. This will help expand the industry and create more employment opportunities.

### 7. Improve Cybersecurity Framework
Strong cybersecurity policies should be implemented to protect client data. Secure systems increase international trust in Bangladeshi outsourcing services.

## 6. Conclusion

*Outsourcing has become an important sector for economic development in Bangladesh. With a young workforce, government support, and growing technological infrastructure, the country has great potential to become a global outsourcing hub. However, challenges such as skill gaps, payment issues, and infrastructure limitations must be addressed to fully utilize this opportunity. By investing in education, improving connectivity, and strengthening policy support, Bangladesh can significantly expand its presence in the global outsourcing market and create sustainable employment for millions of people. Additional Related Quotations “Outsourcing is not just about reducing cost; it is about accessing global talent.” — Thomas H. Davenport, Harvard Business Review “Digital skills and freelancing opportunities can transform developing economies like Bangladesh.” — Oxford Internet Institute Report (2023) “The future workforce will increasingly work beyond borders through digital outsourcing.” — International Labour Organization (ILO)*

title: Cashless Society in Bangladesh
titleBn: ক্যাশলেস সোসাইটি বিনির্মাণ ও আর্থিক অন্তর্ভুক্তি

quotation.quote: Digital payments are critical to the government’s vision.
quotation.author:
National Digital
Payments Roadmap | Bangladesh 2022–2025

introduction: A cashless society is a system in which most payments are made through digital tools such as mobile wallets, bank transfers, cards, QR codes, and online platforms instead of physical cash. In Bangladesh, this shift is being shaped by the National Digital Payments Roadmap, the spread of mobile financial services, wider mobile and internet access, and a government target to move all transactions under a cashless system by 2031. At the same time, Bangladesh is still in transition rather than fully cashless. UNDP Bangladesh, citing the 2025 World Bank Global Findex, reports that 34 percent of adults made or received a digital payment in 2024, 43 percent had an account, 82 percent owned a mobile phone, and 44 percent used the internet; yet Bangladesh Bank’s payment-system data, as reported by The Business Standard, showed that 71.72 percent of transaction value in December 2024 was still cash-based. (UNDP)

prospects.title: A very large mobile base can accelerate digital payments. Bangladesh had
prospects.explanation: 185 million mobile connections and 77.7 million internet users at the start of 2025, which gives digital payment providers a broad platform for wallet, app, and QR-based services. As connectivity improves, more people can move from cash to low-cost mobile transactions. (DataReportal – Global Digital Insights)

prospects.title: Mobile financial services are already operating at national scale. In
prospects.explanation: Bangladesh Bank’s May 2024 snapshot, MFS had 879.78 lakh active accounts, more than 606.8 million monthly transactions, and transaction value above Tk 141,612 crore. That scale shows that digital payments are already part of everyday economic life, not just a niche service. (BB)

prospects.title: Government-led digitization can pull millions into formal payments. The
prospects.explanation: national roadmap states that government payments were already 26 percent digital by volume and 58 percent by value, and that the government had digitized 100 percent of wage payments to employees. When public payments move digitally, citizens and businesses gain stronger incentives to keep using formal channels.

prospects.title: Interoperability is improving the payment ecosystem. Bangladesh’s
prospects.explanation: National Payment Switch Bangladesh (NPSB) processed more than 15.4 crore transactions worth Tk 2.71 lakh crore in 2024, and Bangla QR now integrates 43 banks, five MFS providers, and three payment service providers. This kind of interoperability can reduce friction and make digital payments more convenient across institutions. (Daily Sun)

prospects.title: Digital wages can strengthen women’s economic participation. UNDP
prospects.explanation: argues that digital wages can improve control over earnings, open accounts, and build credit histories for women workers. In a country where many women still work in vulnerable or informal conditions, payment digitization can become a tool of empowerment as well as efficiency. (UNDP)

prospects.title: The economic gains could be significant. Better Than Cash Alliance
prospects.explanation: estimated that digitizing payments could add 1.7 percent to Bangladesh’s annual GDP, equivalent to about US$6.2 billion a year. That suggests cashless expansion is not only a financial-sector reform but also a growth strategy. (Better Than Cash Alliance)

prospects.title: Bangladesh already has a structured policy roadmap. The 2022–2025
prospects.explanation: National Digital Payments Roadmap identifies 22 solutions for a safe, interoperable, and inclusive payment ecosystem across ready-made garments, retail, agriculture, health, and education. This gives the country a policy foundation for moving from scattered digital use to a more coordinated cashless system. (Better Than Cash Alliance)

challenges.title: Cash still dominates the economy. Bangladesh Bank’s payment data showed
challenges.explanation: that 71.72 percent of transaction value in December 2024 was in cash, and more than 72 percent of all monetary transactions were still conducted in cash according to the central bank’s latest report as covered by The Business Standard. This means the country is far from replacing cash in large parts of the economy. (The Business Standard)

challenges.title: Access is wider than active usage. UNDP’s summary of the 2025 World
challenges.explanation: Bank Global Findex shows a gap between ownership and use: 82 percent of adults own a mobile phone, but only 44 percent use the internet and 34 percent made or received a digital payment in 2024. So infrastructure exists more widely than confident, regular digital-payment behavior. (UNDP)

challenges.title: Cash-out costs remain a major barrier. The roadmap says service-cost

Topic 17: Cashless Society in Bangladesh
Quotation

“Digital payments are critical to the government’s vision.” — National Digital
Payments Roadmap | Bangladesh 2022–2025

Introduction

A cashless society is a system in which most payments are made through digital
tools such as mobile wallets, bank transfers, cards, QR codes, and online platforms
instead of physical cash. In Bangladesh, this shift is being shaped by the National
Digital Payments Roadmap, the spread of mobile financial services, wider mobile
and internet access, and a government target to move all transactions under a
cashless system by 2031.

At the same time, Bangladesh is still in transition rather than fully cashless. UNDP
Bangladesh, citing the 2025 World Bank Global Findex, reports that 34 percent of
adults made or received a digital payment in 2024, 43 percent had an account, 82
percent owned a mobile phone, and 44 percent used the internet; yet Bangladesh
Bank’s payment-system data, as reported by The Business Standard, showed that
71.72 percent of transaction value in December 2024 was still cash-based. (UNDP)

Relative Data (Selected recent indicators)

                   Indicator                               Figure              Period
 Mobile connections                                 185 million             Early 2025
 Internet users                                     77.7 million            January
